question: Let $f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to\{2,4,6,8,10\}$ be defined by $f(x)=2x$. Determine whether two distinct elements of the domain can have the same image under $f$.
explanation:
Step 1: To test the one-one property, consider two elements $x_1,x_2$ of the domain such that $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$.
Step 2: Using $f(x)=2x$, we get $2x_1=2x_2$.
Step 3: Dividing both sides by $2$ gives $x_1=x_2$.
Step 4: Thus, equality of images is possible only when the corresponding elements of the domain are equal.
Step 5: Therefore, no two distinct elements of the domain have the same image.
Final Answer: The function is one-one.

options.B: Yes; every element of the codomain has two pre-images
options.C: No; the mapping does not define a function
